findings.evidence: "Only changing the attention mechanism itself (e.g., hybrid/linear attention) can reduce the growth rate: the layers it replaces hold a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing per-token cache, so a hybrid that still keeps some full-attention layers keeps growing — only more slowly — and only a model with no full-attention layers stops growing entirely (Ch 7, Fig 7.2) — KV offload changes where the cache resides, not how fast it grows."
findings.issue: Dense run-on sentence (three em-dashes, three nested clauses) obscures the load-bearing distinction. It is difficult to parse whether 'only more slowly' refers to hybrid models or to the model with no full-attention layers.
findings.fix_instruction: Split into two sentences: 'Only changing the attention mechanism can reduce the growth rate. A hybrid that keeps some full-attention layers grows more slowly; only a model with no full-attention layers stops growing entirely (Ch 7, Fig 7.2). KV offload changes where the cache resides, not how fast it grows.'
